newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds shake off losses, end up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds shake off losses, end up.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds regained lost ground and then some to end Tuesday's session higher, mirroring U.S. Treasury and equity markets which also reversed early losses to close higher, dealers said.
Shortcovering in an oversold market and a slightly weak Redbook retail sales index fueled Treasuries, dealers said.
High-grade corporate bond dealers said spreads across most maturities held firm and volume was weak.
"It was a very slow day to start the week off," said one corporate bond trader, pointing to the thin volume in both junk and investment-grade trading arenas.
Reebok International Ltd debt was unchanged despite news Moody's cut its senior unsecured debt rating to Baa2 from A3 and affirmed its Prime-2 commercial paper rating.
Dealers said Reebok debt is a rarity in secondary trade.
In the high-yield market, prices closed unchanged to up 1/8 despite falling about one point early in the session, dealers said.
News last week that ValuJet Inc airplanes will return to the skies in two to three weeks continued to boost the airline's debt.
ValuJet's 10.25 percent debt due 2001 gained about 3/4 of a point to close at 89-1/4 offer. The notes gained more than a point last Friday.
Grocery sector paper weakened with Bruno paper ending off at 101 bid, while Ralphs Grocery Co 11.0 percent paper was bid lower at 96-3/4, 97-1/2 offer, traders said.
In retail paper, Penn Traffic's 9.625 percent paper traded off 1-1/2 points to 67-1/4 bid, traders added.
Stratosphere Corp's 14.25 percent paper traded up 2-1/2 points on the offer side at a 81-1/2 bid, 83-1/2 offer.
The notes shed over four points on Friday after news Stratosphere suspended construction on its new hotel tower due to an anticipated cash shortfall, dealers said.
In the new issue arena, no deals are yet seen coming to market this week, but a handful of junk deals are scheduled to kick-off road shows.
First Nationwide Escrow Corp will hit the road to sell $525 million of senior subordinated notes due 2003 via Smith Barney Inc.
Use of proceeds is to fund the $1.2 billion announced acquisition of California Federal Bancorp Inc.
Also, Euramax International Ltd is looking to place $125 million of 10-year senior subordinated notes via JP Morgan Securities Inc.
The 30-year long bond was up 25/32 at 96-0732 to yield 7.05 percent in late trade Tuesday. The Dow Jones Industrials Average closed up 32.18 at 5648.39.
